transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
My wife thinks I’m not eating enough. Most days I’ll have coffee and toast in the morning, then maybe some soup or vegetables later on. Big meals just feel unnecessary to me at my age.
Do you usually feel hungry?
Not especially. I eat what seems enough to me—coffee and toast in the morning, then perhaps soup or some vegetables later. Big meals just don’t feel necessary at my age.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I’m not sure I’d call it depression. I’ve just been going about my usual routine.
Have you lost weight recently without trying to?
My doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low. I suppose I have gotten lighter, but it feels easier getting around the garden and keeping up with my walks that way.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes, I do, a bit. When my wife puts butter on things or serves me a full plate, I get nervous I’ll start putting the weight back on and lose the control I’ve managed to keep.
Do you feel overweight, even though others say you are too thin?

I don’t think of myself as overweight exactly, but if my belt is a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. And if I catch my stomach looking even a little rounded in the mirror, I feel sloppy and disappointed.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a much larger amount of food than most people would in a similar time?
No, I don’t think so. I eat fairly small amounts, really.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I haven’t done that.
Do you use laxatives, diet pills, or excessive exercise to keep your weight down?
I’m not sure what you’d count as excessive exercise. I do try to stay active, but I don’t use laxatives or diet pills.
What is your current weight?
My doctor says my weight has gotten too low. I don’t have the number in my head, but I feel like being lighter helps me get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Has your weight dropped to a level your doctor said is dangerously low for your height?

Yes, that’s what my doctor has said—the number on the scale is too low for me. I suppose I understand that, but being lighter does make it easier for me to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
